objective: Deciding what happens when a Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, and who may cancel a Sprint
secondaryObjectives: Adapting the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint without endangering the Sprint Goal
Engaging stakeholders and customers through the Sprint Review and the Product Owner without taking the plan from the Developers
Managing the Product Backlog as an emergent, ordered list and judging when an item is ready for selection

brief.situation: You are the Scrum Master of the loyalty team at Harbor Lane Outfitters, a fictional online outdoor-gear shop. Sprint 9 runs one week, Monday 1 March to Friday 5 March 2027. Its Sprint Goal: members can redeem points for a discount at checkout. The points scheme is run with a partner bank.
handover: Developers: Sam, Ana and Joe. Product Owner: Maya. Dana, VP of Sales, is keen on anything that helps the spring promotion.
Sprint Backlog: 16 points across three items, all serving the Sprint Goal.
howItWorks: The dashboard shows the commitments, the board, the burn-down, issues, the people and the events. Decisions come to you as the week unfolds; between them you can act from the action groups.
Move the week on when you are ready. Each morning the board shows what the Developers finished the day before.
When the Sprint ends, by cancellation or at the Review, you decide with the team what happens to its work and write a short reflection.

reflection.question: Reflect on the Sprint: how the team handled the bigger item and Dana's request, what an obsolete Sprint Goal called for and who decided, and what happened to the work.

parts.label: Inside the Sprint
parts.criteria: Scope renegotiated with the Product Owner without lowering quality or stretching the Sprint; a stakeholder's new request routed to the Product Owner and the Product Backlog, not pulled into the Sprint round her.
parts.modelAnswer: When redeeming points turned out bigger, the Developers and Maya renegotiated scope: a slice that still met the Sprint Goal, the rest back to the Product Backlog; quality and the Sprint's length did not move. Dana's gift-card request went to Maya, who orders the Product Backlog; nothing was added that endangered the Goal.

parts.label: The obsolete Goal
parts.criteria: Recognized the Sprint Goal as obsolete, brought the facts to the Product Owner at once, and left the cancellation to her (only the Product Owner may cancel); Done work kept and inspected, undone items returned to the Product Backlog; nothing undone released.
parts.modelAnswer: Once the bank ended the scheme, the Sprint Goal was obsolete. I brought Maya the facts straight away and she cancelled the Sprint: only the Product Owner has that authority. We kept and inspected the Done work, returned the undone items to the Product Backlog for her to re-order, and planned a new Sprint.

expertPath.text: Have the Developers and Maya renegotiate the bigger item's scope; the Sprint Goal, quality and the Sprint's length stay.

adapted.headline: Good: inspected, adapted, and the right person decided
adapted.body: Scope moved, quality did not; Dana's request went to the Product Owner; and when the Goal became obsolete, Maya cancelled the Sprint at once.

partly.headline: The right call, with gaps
partly.body: Maya cancelled the Sprint, but the criteria below show where the week cost the team: stretched or overloaded, a request pulled in round the Product Owner, or work thrown away.

smCancelled.headline: Not the Scrum Master's call
smCancelled.body: 'Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel the Sprint' (Scrum Guide 2020). Bring her the facts; she decides.

shipped.headline: Undone work released
shipped.body: Work that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be released; it returns to the Product Backlog.

qualityCut.headline: Quality traded for time
qualityCut.body: 'Quality does not decrease' during the Sprint. When work is bigger than expected, scope is renegotiated with the Product Owner.

wasted.headline: The Goal was obsolete, and the Sprint ran on
wasted.body: An obsolete Sprint Goal is the case for cancelling the Sprint. Building on, or rewriting the Goal mid-Sprint, wastes the rest of it.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: The Sprint was not closed before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Inside the Sprint, scope is renegotiated with the Product Owner when work turns out bigger, while the Sprint Goal, quality and the Sprint's length hold; stakeholders change the Product Backlog by convincing the Product Owner. When the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, the Sprint can be cancelled, and only the Product Owner has that authority: bring her the facts at once. Keep and inspect the Done work, return the undone items to the Product Backlog, and plan a new Sprint.
